en: Now, as you can tell, if you take a look at
the official HTMX reference page,
HTMX offers quite a few
attributes you can add and some other
features which we'll also explore throughout
this course.
And whilst I won't cover all those
attributes in this section here already,
since this is just the essentials section,
there is one other really essential
attribute that I do wanna cover here, and
that's the hx-trigger attribute.
And the hx-trigger attribute can be added to
an element
to control how exactly the request will be
triggered.
So hx-get defines
which kind of request,
a GET request to this path should be sent,
and hx-trigger then configures
when that request should be sent, so how it
should be triggered.
And of course,
it worked without that attribute as well,
right? A request was sent when we clicked
the button. And the reason for that is that
by default,
requests will be sent when the most obvious
event, you could say, the event that makes
the most sense for a given element occurs.
For example, for a form,
that would be the submit event. For a
button, and actually for most elements, it's
a click event.
And therefore, if you wanna send that
request upon a click
on the element on which the attribute is
added,
you don't need hx-trigger.
But you do need it if you wanna send the
request when some other event occurs.
And you can configure quite a lot of things
here. You can, for example, also make sure
that it's
a click event with the Control key pressed.
That could be done as well. And you see the
syntax for that here in the docs, though you
of course don't need to go through them
here. I'll show you some important examples
here throughout this course.
So let's therefore say that here for demo
purposes,
I wanna send the request if I
enter
this element with my mouse, so if I hover
over it,
if I also at the same time have the Control
key pressed.
If I save that all
and I reload here, you'll notice that if I
now
mouse over Learn More, nothing happens.
If I click it,
nothing happens.
But if I now hold the Control key, which I'm
now doing,
and I hover over it, now the request was
sent and this is loaded.
Now you can also define multiple events that
should trigger this request simply by
separating them with a comma here in that
value for hx-trigger.
So for example, here we could also add
click.
And now this would make sure that this
request here is sent whenever we mouse over
the button, if the Control key is pressed,
or if we just click the button without the
requirement of the Control key being
pressed.
And with that, if I save that, if I reload
this page,
you'll notice that if I hover over it,
nothing happens.
If I hover over it with the Control key
pressed, this is loaded,
and if I click it, this is also loaded.
And that's how you can use hx-trigger to
configure in detail
when
exactly that request is sent. You don't need
it if you're happy with the default, which
in most cases is a click,
but if you have some other specific event
for which the request should be sent,
hx-trigger is your friend.
